data.question_intent: Interpretation of market data and RWA efficiency
data.question_quote: One, maybe an uncomfortable question, on Dealogic data and the quarterly run rate at the moment. It does look pretty weak, it did look pretty weak in Q1 and then it turned out to be okay. Obviously April was quite a meaningful month. So I'm guess I'm trying to ask for some help to how to think about that market data that's coming through, because in Q1 it turned out to be, I think, wrong. So if there's any hand holding you can do there to help us interpret the data.
data.answer_quote: In terms of Dealogic data, clearly there is a subdued Banking environment. We saw that through Q1 and it's, if anything, more intense in April and particularly in ECM and M&A, there's probably a lot less activity than perhaps people expected at the beginning of the year. From our perspective, we planned for a market that was 10% down year-on-year. Q1 was broadly in alignment with that. What we have focused our businesses on is, clearly the scale of the market will go up and down. We are focusing them on making the market share gains that we've asked them to make, so even in a lower market [environment], are they making progress? So that's how we are thinking about it. And so far, we would say that things are getting postponed [and] pushed out, rather than cancelled. So that's what we see. There's just uncertainty in the market and therefore you can imagine the CEO community are reluctant to progress. It's very difficult to say anything more than that.
data.reason: The answer directly addresses the question's intent, providing a high-level interpretation of the market data and RWA efficiency, with a clear stance and alignment with the narrative. It includes numeric evidence of a 10% year-on-year market decline and discusses the impact on business focus and market share gains.
